sources.evidence: Our copy is an issue of the Imperial College newspaper Felix cut off at exactly 1,048,576 bytes with no page index, so only the first page image can be read, and that page (Union planning group news, copyright line FELIX 1985) does not mention a programming contest.

Page 4 of this 15-page issue of Felix (Friday 24 January) carries a news item 'All Four Won' about an Imperial College team that won the European finals of the ACM programming contest in November and qualified for the world finals; the issue holds no results table.

erc-1987.notes: The item prints no year, so it cannot be tied to 1987 from the text alone; the address is a Koninklijke Bibliotheek newspaper resolver link, whose issue date is not in our copy. Check the issue date against the 1987 contest.

sources.evidence: A 638-byte text of a Dutch newspaper item about a team that came second in a European programming contest in London with 17 teams; it gives no ranking of other teams and prints no year.

erc-1988.notes: The wayback copy of ERC88.pdf in the same archive folder (20240413) is cut off at 1,048,576 bytes; the 2026-10-23 copy is the complete one and is the one described.

sources.evidence: Cover and every problem page read 'European Regional Finals of the 1988-89 ACM Scholastic Programming Contest', November 12, 1988, with seven problems A to G.
